evidence.quote: Scientists determined the three-dimensional position of more than 23,000 atoms in a tiny iron-platinum particle with 22 picometer precision.

claims.statement: Scientists determined the positions of more than 23,000 atoms in a tiny iron-platinum particle with 22 picometer precision.

evidence.quote: scientists determined the 3D coordinates of 6,569 iron and 16,627 platinum atoms in an iron-platinum nanoparticle.

claims.statement: The characterized nanoparticle contained 6,569 iron atoms and 16,627 platinum atoms.

evidence.quote: They used an imaging technique called atomic electron tomography to correlate 3D atomic arrangements and chemical order/disorder with material properties at the single-atom level.

claims.statement: Atomic electron tomography was used to correlate 3D atomic arrangements and chemical order/disorder with material properties at the single-atom level.

evidence.quote: They identified rich structural variety and chemical order/disorder with unprecedented 3D detail including atomic composition, grain boundaries, anti-phase boundaries, anti-site point defects and swap defects.

claims.statement: The nanoparticle exhibited rich structural variety and chemical order/disorder, including several types of boundaries and point defects.

evidence.quote: anti-phase boundaries (where atoms are arranged in the opposite order of the perfect, parent crystal)

claims.statement: Anti-phase boundaries are locations where atoms are arranged in the opposite order of the perfect parent crystal.

evidence.quote: swap defects (where individual or a pair of nearest-neighbor atoms switch places)

claims.statement: Swap defects occur when individual atoms or pairs of nearest-neighbor atoms switch places.

evidence.quote: experimentally measured 3D atomic coordinates and chemical species with 22 picometer precision can be used as direct input for first-principles calculations of material properties

claims.statement: Experimentally measured 3D atomic coordinates and chemical species with 22 picometer precision can be used as direct input for first-principles calculations of material properties.

evidence.quote: scientists expect this approach to find broad use in materials science, physics, chemistry, and other fields.

claims.statement: The approach is expected to find broad use in materials science, physics, chemistry, and other fields.

evidence.quote: It also gives researchers the ability to study material properties on the single-atom level that could transform our understanding of structure-property relationships at the most fundamental level.

claims.statement: The approach enables study of material properties at the single-atom level and may transform understanding of structure-property relationships at the most fundamental level.
